title: Winter warmth gave no clear link to first-to-full cherry bloom intervals in four Japan samples from 1953 to 2021
abstract: We tested whether warmer winters were linked to longer intervals from first to full cherry bloom in Japan. We joined JMA phase dates to fixed-calendar temperature measures from a published campaign dataset. We used 4,436 paired station-years at 71 stations with at least 15 records in both periods. Four models split records at 36 N and at 1988. Each model controlled for spring temperature, station effects, and year effects. Winter slopes ranged from -0.010 to +0.489 days per C. All four adjusted uncertainty intervals included zero. In southern samples, both phase dates had positive winter slopes, but their difference remained uncertain. These results do not establish an interval response or a chilling mechanism. The sample omits years without complete source weather and bloom records. Tree changes, visit timing, and weather error remain possible sources of bias.

display.caption: Winter-temperature slopes for the first-to-full cherry bloom interval. Bars use a four-test Bonferroni correction and two-way station and year cluster covariance.
